query: Browser 2.5D melee brawler in Three.js: a true 3D timber workshop terrace fought on one lateral z=0 plane. Camera: locked perspective at (0,3.1,15.4) looking at (0,2.0,0), 32° FOV; no orbit, follow, pan or zoom; screen-left is always −X. Controls: Left/Right walks or punches an in-range attacker, repeats within 240 ms climb combo tiers 1–4; Down crouch, Up jump, second Up air-step, Down-then-Up uppercut, airborne Down dive-strike, a key throws the weapon; touch parity. Loop: attackers walk in from both gutter arches while hazards cross above — props to crouch under or jump over, riders low enough to uppercut or high enough to need a throw, plus a melee-immune shuttered emitter a throw silences. Unbroken combos multiply coin payout funding permanent unlocks; weapons have swing durability and a throw spends one whole. Three ordered arenas each close with a telegraphed mallet foreman before endless endurance opens; zero health ends the run. Procedural bevelled cartoon geometry in warm sun-bleached timber: boarded deck, sided wall, rooftop tiers, foreground crops; player-only teal accent, hazard-only red.

2.5D browser deduction game in three.js/WebGL2: a real 3D desk scene — matte handheld dialing device on an angled cradle, neutral desaturated interior, and a recessed self-lit screen whose emission level carries call state as the only animated light. Camera: locked, elevated frontal-oblique; the device fills ~60% of frame height; screen and key grid stay within 6° of parallel; no orbit, zoom, or drift, only a child node shaking 0.008 units on rejection, returning to zero. Controls: click modeled keys or keyboard. Loop: knowing only 4180, dial a 4-digit code, watch DIALING→RINGING→CONNECTED, advance comedic dialogue one line per input while flagged lines write digit-fragment clue cards, then combine two cards, sometimes re-calling an unlocked contact for a conditional follow-up, to deduce the next code and open one of five directory rows up to a terminal call. A locked contact's code gives the same UNAVAILABLE notice as any unassigned code, so guessing ahead cannot skip the chain. No timer, score, or fail state; dialogue is selectable DOM text on the projected screen rect, not 3D meshes.

Build Frostline Battery, a Three.js/WebGL2 fixed-emplacement anti-air shooter: a stationary gunner defends a snow-bound industrial town from escalating aerial raids. Camera: rotating rig anchored at the gunner pivot, pointer-locked, yaw 360°, pitch clamped about -12° to +82°, never inverted, never translating. The centered reticle is the hit ray, with no aim assist, so leading is the skill: LMB fires the left gun, RMB the right, each with its own heat and overheat lockout; Space/E triggers an ability (air-burst barrage or overdrive, the second unlocked by upgrade). Loop: pre-wave threat preview and countdown → combat as raiders, gunships and bombers converge from many bearings and altitudes, kills paying resources while completed attack runs cut town integrity → cursor upgrade panel for guns, abilities and repair → next wave. Zero integrity is defeat, clearing the campaign is victory, both through results to restart. Fill every reachable orientation: foreground twin barrels, settlement with sweeping searchlights, volumetric overcast sky dome, ridgeline and drifting snow, never an empty plane. The world stays cold desaturated blue-grey; warm color belongs to muzzle flash, tracers, explosions and fire. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled or higher-segment silhouettes; if adopted, keep background props economical.

2D side-view foundry run-and-gun: swap mouse-aimed guns through drone waves to a crane boss's glowing core. If a generated sprite sheet is used, it is the default rendering; procedural art remains an internal failure fallback, never player-facing.

Fixed single-screen 2D top-down pixel art: a brass lantern automaton clears violet ink wisps from a midnight archive arena. Move 8-way; short jumps dodge contact and only landing pulses kill. Three health, ten stages of waves.

A 2D pixel-art boss shooter, fixed side-on view of an orbital salvage yard: a stationary platform click-fires at four harmless colossi, one per 20-second clock. Crit drifting amber weak points and shoot passing boosts for brief fire-rate or damage buffs; win or lose, tokens upgrade both.

Build Long Watch, a first-person 3D horror caretaking game (Three.js/WebGL2, React DOM UI): one night tending an elderly wheelchair-bound resident in a dim old timber house. Camera: first person only, never fixed, third-person or 2.5D; movement camera-relative, A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted or axis-swapped. Controls: WASD, Shift jog, Ctrl crouch, E interact/hold, Q stow lamp; gaze-only interaction via a rim-glow reticle. Loop: each of three shifts issues duties, so search rooms and drawers for the needed item, then return and perform one of five care actions (hand water, give medication, straighten floor bedding, close a window, dock the wheelchair); two-handed actions require stowing the lamp, and clearing a shift unlocks more rooms. Escalation reveals missing supplies and opens a night street navigable only by its chain of sodium light pools, rewritten on the return. Back inside, one unfightable threat hunts by sight and sound, lamp and room lights widening its detection: crouch, go dark, hide in a closet. Contact or 60s of untended pain rolls back to the nearest checkpoint with progress intact; dawn resolves as Clean or Broken Handover. Look: rectangular lattice of paper sliding doors, matte wood and plaster at 8-25% value, cool-white textiles the brightest silhouettes, the handheld lamp the only shadow caster; backlit paper shows silhouettes before a door opens. One full-screen analog degradation pass (scanlines, channel offset, per-line jitter, vignette) scaled by max(shift baseline, threat proximity) is the sole danger readout.

Hand-painted 2D visual novel: a student becomes the singing Tuner; choice-raised bond buffs combat; battles end only when stability drain opens a Faint and a purify chart fills. Optionally a generated sprite sheet; if used it is the default visible rendering, procedural art an internal failure fallback only, never player-facing.

2D top-down pixel CRPG in a rain-soaked toxic city; pan-only camera on a 32px grid, all art drawn procedurally. Loop: hub → travel → explore → dialogue d20 checks branching on success/partial/failure → mission by stealth, force, or 4-symbol code deduction → rewards and upgrades, four chapters to four endings. Debt installments, faction standing, and heat interlock; night and acid rain shrink a stepped vision radius.

2D cut-paper collage: greyscale, one signal hue per chapter, emblem faces and notes. Per chapter: walk sideways, talk, solve a cross-scene puzzle, then the camera locks for a four-lane arrow-key rhythm set; heat multiplies score, misses cost lives, grades rewrite each song into a final suite. Optional generated player sprite sheet; if adopted it is the default rendering, procedural art only an internal fallback, never player-facing.

Build a browser 2.5D timed worker-dispatch management game: a true 3D hand-painted gouache Three.js diorama under a locked isometric OrthographicCamera. Camera: frustum height 22, yaw 45°, pitch 35.264°; no orbit, pan, zoom or worker-following, only a ≤4px shake that numerically resets. Input: click or tap only, raycast interactables, else project to y=0 and snap within 1.5 tiles. Loop: grab surface piles of supply, timber, stone, coin and crystal → spend them clearing tiered gates, each clear unlocking the adjacent tile and everything on it → repair damaged production buildings → collect their 8s batches → buy two upgrade tiers → calm or drive off giant creatures and rifts as timed tasks, never combat, no health bars → activate objective devices, one adding a cross-layer path → finish 3–4 objectives before a 180–260s countdown, ≥40%/≥15%/>0 remaining scoring 3/2/1 stars. 2–4 workers walk 3.2 tiles/s with travel on the clock, orders queue up to 4, and clicks validate unoccupied→reachable→affordable→free worker, naming the first failure and deducting nothing; a 20s-regenerating pile keeps levels solvable. Single-screen levels stay genuinely height-layered: terraced cliffs, bridges, sunken emissive molten flow and cloud sea, procedural geometry over raw primitives, foreground occluders at the frame edges, hazed distance, a directional key light grounding every interactable. A screen-constant neutral outline marks clickability, inverting to a dark inner stroke in the pale isle chapter; occluders covering a worker ghost to semi-transparent silhouettes and never absorb clicks.

2D card duel for three locations. Mana rises over six rounds; both sides place pages face down, then reveal at once — same-slot cards trade attack into health and higher attack holds the location. Most held wins; 12-card decks between matches. Dark painted manuscript tabletop. Card art may be generated; if so, keep UI and text code-native.

Build Allegiance Shift Arena, a browser first-person arena shooter in true 3D (Three.js/WebGL2): every hit is instantly lethal and the victim respawns in the killer's faction, so faction size is the score.
Camera: head-locked first person, FOV 95° widening to 100° at top speed, pitch clamped ±85°; the viewmodel sits on an overlay layer and never clips walls.
Controls: pointer-lock look, click fire, Space jump; WASD from camera yaw on XZ — A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted or swapped.
Loop: ground cap 8.5m/s; each tangential air-input strafe-jump adds +0.9m/s to a hard 17m/s cap, and rejumping within 120ms of landing preserves speed, read only as grid smear along the horizontal velocity vector, never a number. Firing casts one non-penetrating 120m ray on a 0.55s cooldown; no aim assist. Kills dissolve the target into shards and shift the proportional faction bar. Death just respawns you clear of enemies with brief fire-cancelled protection. 180s match, 8 fighters, up to 4 factions, largest wins.
Arena: sealed 62×62×12m interior, looping corridors, pillars every 6m, two platform tiers with jumpable gaps, one lethal pit. Environment and UI stay hue-free greyscale — pale grid-lined walls, near-black pillars, matte, no fog or bloom — saturation only on faction fills and tracers. Every camera angle must frame structure — trusses, pilasters, ribs — not blank planes.

First-person timed-shift shooter in a sealed automated assembly complex (Three.js/WebGL2): ready three subsystems and package one prototype before a 600 s countdown expires. Camera: head-locked, FOV 60, pitch clamped ±80°, never third-person; the handheld tool renders on a separate FOV 45 layer. Controls: pointer-lock look, WASD from camera forward/right projected onto XZ so A strafes screen-left, Shift sprint, hold fire, E pick up/submit, F start/check/package. Loop: gather three part types (carry cap 3), submit at the matching station, then guard its stepped 12 s process — a drone within 4 m regresses progress 6%/s; the acoustic station instead ends in a sweeping level meter where F must land in the −18..−6 dB band, overshoot locking it 4 s. Spiked drones stream from wall vents and drain stamina on contact; each takes ~1.7 s of sustained beam, and overheat locks firing 1.5 s. Each readiness raises spawn pressure; all three light the hub pad, where holding F 3 s packages and a hit zeroes the hold. Countdown or stamina zero ends in a scored settlement. Low-poly cartoon sci-fi bays, one dominant hue each around a neutral hub, height fog, mirror floors, and a crawling-outline grid interference layer scaling with drone count; the near-white beam is the sole peak brightness against dark orange-red-spiked drones.

2D fixed-camera single-screen pixel horror adventure; no pan or zoom. Arrow keys walk a pale creature; typed verb-noun commands examine, take, combine, and open item-gated exits between static scenes. Clues raise truth_progress toward the ending; fatal acts rewind to the last save. 16-color dithered red terrain, green sky, framed parser panel.

Top-down pixel-art: a tiny stray pushes crates one tile, never pulling, to clear alley grid puzzles. Exits unlock on their puzzle plus a clue won by gifting strays. Hunger decays and drains health at zero; forage bins, hunt prey; undo/reset frees deadlocks. Camera follows, snapping to the grid. Oversized clutter dwarfs it under warm lamp halos.

Build a Three.js/WebGL 3D colony-management sim on a temperate coastal island. Camera: elevated three-quarter bird's-eye, pitch 35–60°, WASD/drag pan on camera-forward/right axes (A moves screen-left, D screen-right), clamped scroll zoom, Q/E 90° yaw snaps that never invert left/right, F eased recenter. Loop: place grid-snapped, road-adjacent buildings → assign villagers across 8 professions → run chains logs→planks, grain→bread, ore→tools/weapons, where a missing input stalls a building → hunger, energy, health and warmth drive auto-eating, gold auto-buys, rest and illness, halving output when unmet → births and deaths shift labor → a Warm↔Cold toggle drains warmth, cuts yields and lays snow → trade with a visiting trader and dispatch trade or exploration ships at Low/Medium/High risk → a rising stockpile threshold spawns a raider wave that towers, walls and paid units repel before it loots the stores → each interval pick 1 of 3 enhancement cards to use or bank, 3 carrying into the next run. Pause/1x/2x/4x scale one fixed tick. Population 0 or starvation ends the run into a summary and a fresh map. Matte flat-shaded low-poly, signature terracotta roofs, faceted teal water, snow masking up-facing surfaces while facet edges stay crisp, sun key with contact shadows, and dense instanced scatter filling every camera corner under a dark translucent HUD that stays off terracotta. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props beveled higher-segment custom geometry, keeping background props economical.

Three.js/WebGL2 over-the-shoulder tactical squad shooter: lead four operatives through humid rainforest and vine-clad concrete ruins against an invented ochre-tagged faction, carrying precision, suppression and launcher weapons. Camera: ~3.2 m behind the chest at 1.75 m, damped, FOV 55 tightening to 38 on aim, pitch −55°…+35°, sphere-swept pull-in at walls, occluding foliage fading; never top-down or orthographic. Controls: WASD strictly camera-relative on separate axes (W screen-forward, A screen-left, never inverted), sprint, crouch and prone, LMB fire, hold RMB aim, Q mark a hostile or point, F1–F4 order squadmates to follow, hold, advance to marker or cease fire. Loop: loadout, then a free-look insertion flight whose chosen drop point sets the starting alert; crouched recon where stance and foliage govern both spread and enemy recognition; raycast firefights where rock stops bullets, planks do not and smoke blocks only sight, alert climbing undetected→suspicious→engaged, propagating between groups and calling reinforcements; chained capture, demolition and escort objectives spawning fresh hostiles; a guarded high-value target and an armored car vulnerable at its rear grille; extraction or a timed hold. Downed operatives stay down for the mission and control passes to the nearest survivor; squad wipe, escort loss or timer expiry ends in results that always offer retry with unlocks kept. Low-saturation cool-green grade: one canopy-broken directional key over hemisphere fill, indoor window shafts, exponential fog; every angle must stack near foliage, mid-ground cover and distant cliff silhouettes, never untextured primitives or empty ground. Optionally, where water fills a meaningful part of the view, use animated waves, Fresnel blending and wave-distorted real-time planar reflections, with a static environment map only as an internal fallback.

Build a 2.5D local same-screen party arena brawler in Three.js: four cel-shaded fighters (speed, power, balanced, dash) brawl on a fixed side-view stage — foreground truss framing, midground platform, distant backdrop — in a warm theater, cool rooftop, or neon venue, with thick black outlines, flat toon bands, and identity colors tinting outlines, HUD segments, and pickups. Camera: perspective locked to a slightly elevated (~8° downward) side view framing the combat plane and both boundaries; no orbit, follow, pan, or zoom, only brief impact shake returning to pose. Controls: per-player keyboard groups plus gamepads; left/right drives the plane's X axis, jump with double jump, fast punch, high-knockback kick, direction+attack dash slam, with knockback and hitstun. Loop: lobby (mode, 2–4 players, AI fills empty slots) → character and venue select → countdown → brawl → results → rematch reusing config. Points mode scores hits, pickups, and +2/second holding a contested spotlight zone; Health mode eliminates at 0 HP, last standing wins. Overhead emitters telegraph with striped yellow-black glow before a damaging knockback blast; score/heal/buff pickups go to the first toucher.

2D top-down pixel dungeon crawl on a 32px grid; camera follows the player, no rotation or zoom. WASD move, J attack, K pickaxe breaks tiles and trips switches. Camp heals and saves. Fight chasers and orb turrets, push boxes onto plates, collect 3 shards to open the final door, then beat its phased guardian. 6 hearts; death respawns you at camp.

3D point-and-click puzzle-adventure (Three.js) seen through a security-camera lens: BRACE (force: break/lift heavy objects) and WREN (precision: panels, wiring, narrow gaps) are chained together across four night-yard obstacles. Camera: orthographic isometric ~55° downward from a few fixed observation nodes cycled with Q/E, eased 0.6–1s, each framing both workers and the tether; screen-left/right stays consistent across nodes. Left-click paths the active worker (cyan ground ring); Tab or clicking the partner switches control. Loop: observe, move within a 6-unit tether that clamps and either drags the partner or refuses with taut-chain feedback; apply the matching ability in the obstacle's ordered steps, while the wrong worker gets a locked no-effect response; then a dialogue branch in blue/red speaker bubbles shifts trust −3..+3. Solving it with both past the exit opens the next scene; the last yields a trust-keyed ending. No fail state; R resets a stall, keeping trust. Low-poly beveled forms, cool low-key yard of silos, gantries and pallets, drifting fog, warm sodium pools and red strobes; amber only on the two workers and their chrome chain. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled geometry instead of box-only assembly; keep background props economical if adopted.

A comedic film-noir point-and-click mystery on a seaside amusement boardwalk: a quirky sleuth races to solve a disappearance. Render it 2.5D in Three.js: real 3D geometry with cinematic lighting, pixel-art characters and foreground props as alpha billboards on the focal plane. Camera: one fixed directed pose per scene, gameplay subject in focus, background depth-blurred; no orbit, pan or zoom, only a brief puzzle-success shake returning exactly to pose. Mouse only: click to move, examine hotspots, take and combine items, use them on hotspots, talk to NPCs by topic. Loop: explore → question NPCs → combine and use items to solve the scene puzzle → logged clues gate new hotspots and exits → cinematic transition. Run sunlit boardwalk, neon arcade, blue-red pulsing crime scene and stage venue to one evidence-based accusation; wrong moves draw a comic rejection and stay retryable. Hero props are multi-part beveled geometry, never bare primitives on an empty plane.

Diceweaver: Emberbound Chronicle — a single-player dice roguelike deckbuilder staged as a 2.5D Three.js tabletop diorama on one canvas.
Camera: fixed ~35° top-down view centered on the grid with the dice tray forward; no orbit, pan, or zoom, only a brief impact shake back to the locked pose. Backdrops are single full-bleed 16:9 images, never tiled.
Controls: mouse — click dice, drag cards onto units/tiles by raycasting the fixed play plane, then End Turn.
Loop: roll 4 polyhedral dice with colored symbols → spend matching dice on card costs (one reroll, one carry) → attack, guard, relocate, or summon across two facing 2×3 grids where an occupied front column blocks melee to the back, so relocating opens targets → End Turn, enemies execute telegraphed intents. Clearing the grid pays gold and 1 of 3 offers; a party wipe ends the run. Between fights climb a branching parchment node map toward a boss; event choices shift an allied↔opposed stance meter. Permadeath, new seed and map each run.
Visuals: a fogged desaturated diorama recedes so saturated deep-indigo gold-framed vertical cards and beveled engraved dice dominate; stand-ee billboards on plinths over a felt mat, dense instanced props, a warm key spot over cool fill, contact shadows. Saturated hue only on dice and cost icons; neutral text on gold-bronze scroll chrome. Optionally generate character portraits or card art; if adopted, keep card UI and text code-native.

Browser first-person extraction shooter in Three.js: scavenge a seeded, fog-choked post-industrial quarantine zone and extract. Camera: perspective 65° FOV, unlimited yaw, pitch clamped ±80°, instant mouse look; recoil kick and sprint bob only, never third-person. Controls: camera-relative WASD on the ground plane — A screen-left, D screen-right, W forward, S back, never inverted or axis-swapped — Shift sprint, Ctrl crouch, LMB fire, RMB optic, hold F scavenge. Loop: at the hub buy, upgrade and insure gear, then depart into a seeded zone; hold-scavenge containers for tiered loot into a fixed-cell pack; fire hitscan with attachment-tuned recoil and spread while sprinting and firing widen enemy detection that crouching shrinks; a zone timer runs day→dusk→night, darkening ambient and spawning fast night-creatures; anomaly fields drain HP with cold warp and hide artifacts at their edges; a dog flags caches and threats; holding the extraction ring for 12s extracts, the timer resetting on leaving or damage. Extract to keep and sell everything carried; death returns only insured gear; both loop to the hub. State reads only off a glowing wrist device (HP, timer, currency) and a slotted pack grid — no floating windows. Weathered PBR rust, brick and mud; grey-green day, deep-blue night with isolated warm lamps; depth fog dissolving distant pylons; never a sparse diorama. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled, higher-segment geometry instead of box-only assembly; if adopted, keep background props economical.

First-person 3D horror escape puzzle in a sealed forest cabin (Three.js) where the room and a pixel world on an in-world CRT terminal keep rewriting each other. Camera: FOV 60, eye height 1.6 m, pitch clamped ±75°; WASD moves along camera-forward/right so A goes screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted. E inspects, takes and uses items; E at the terminal dollies to a screen-front view, Esc returns free look. Loop: explore for clues, then run a terminal minigame — guess which of three shuffled cards hides the beacon, or steer a light cursor through a top-down maze for three fragments past patrolling eyes — whose result rewrites reality: a win pops a door lock or lights the chalk floor ring and spawns a key; a loss spawns a fatal trap (floor spikes, or the entity from behind the curtain) that warns 0.6 s before killing. Inversely, snuffed candles change the maze's eye count and rune pickups unlock a harder card round. Death fades to black on a heartbeat, then rolls back to the last checkpoint with unlocked doors kept. The exit choice — destroy the terminal, accept the bargain, or force an escape — plus accumulated deaths and runes routes to three endings. Cold teal and blue-black timber lit only by flickering candle points, soft shadows and low fog, against a fluorescent-green scanlined CRT; palettes must not bleed. Dress foreground, midground and background with vines, furniture and log walls; no empty planes.

Browser 3D cozy animal-rescue shelter sim in Three.js. Camera: damped third-person follow at ~4.5 units, pulling to 1.8 for petting and medical close-ups, free 360° yaw, raycast wall avoidance. Controls: WASD on camera-relative ground axes (A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted), mouse orbit, E interact, B build mode. Loop: fund facilities that set capacity, cleaning and adoption environment → take in an animal → hold six decaying needs (hunger, thirst, joy, sleep, health, cleanliness; under 25 alerts and cuts adoption willingness) by feeding, watering, petting, cleaning → when it sickens, test at the medical station for clues, diagnose, then medicate as cure progress rises against climbing toxicity that forces a pause → hire staff to auto-cycle chores for wages → visitors weigh trait match, need satisfaction and environment; clearing the threshold pays funds and reputation and frees the home → close the day to settle finances, swing day-night light, and spawn arrivals. Open-ended, no elimination; neglect only lowers visitor quality; persist to localStorage. Render a dense warm wood-and-cream interior of fabric mats, mesh enclosures, a cool-white tiled medical corner and windows onto forested hills, with drifting dust and soft shadows; the animal is the hero mesh, its rim-lit fur brightening when petted. HUD text stays near-black on light cards; no bare primitives or empty planes.

First-person 3D dungeon-horror crawler in Three.js: advance through a near-black corridor, inspecting lit objects to push a subtitled narrative until frontal threats ambush you into turn-based directional combat.
Camera: eye ~1.6 m; exploration only steps one corridor cell and yaws 90°, moving along camera-forward/right so a visible-left input never moves right; combat locks a fixed face-off framing, no orbit.
Controls: W/S step, A/D turn, E inspect; combat: Up guard, Left/Right attacks, matching arrow counters, Z mash, 1–3 items.
Loop: Normal or Hard scales threat stagger and item counts → advance → inspect to unlock the next gate → a jumpscare locks you into alternating turns: attacks drain its stagger pool, its turns raise Dread or cut Composure, matched counters and mash thresholds negate hits and lower Dread, failures raise it, max Dread forces a hit. Composure 0 respawns at the last checkpoint; the final clear plays an ending, then a bonus segment or other-difficulty restart.
Look: grainy low-fidelity pseudo-3D, near-black space lit by single local points, wet grime, always-enclosing walls and fogged capped ends; the pale threat silhouette is the brightest element, built from layered shells, not primitives. Combat overlays dark-red scanlines pulsing with Dread; red appears nowhere else.

Build Hearthollow Meadows, a cozy 3D open-world life sim in Three.js/WebGL, in soft hand-painted beveled volumes and warm matte materials. Camera: third-person over-shoulder, slight downward tilt, mouse-drag orbit (free yaw, clamped pitch), wheel zoom; never inverted or top-down. Controls: camera-relative WASD (A screen-left, D screen-right), E interact, B build, Q/E rotate, LMB/RMB place/cancel. Loop: harvest highlighted nodes and hit fishing/bug timing windows that retry freely → craft goods and build parts at a workbench → grid-snap parts on the home plot with red/green validity under a decor cap → tend crops and companions, where neglect only slows yield → gift and quest villagers so relation milestones unlock recipes, a mount and regions → ride into waterside dunes, grove and ruin highlands as seasons swap forageables. Persist home, inventory, relations and progress; no combat, death or reset. Warm low-angle key sun, cool fill and haze; no bare plane at any orbit angle. Optionally for the waterside water: animated waves, Fresnel blending and wave-distorted real-time planar reflections; if adopted these are the default rendering with a static environment map only as an internal failure fallback, never a player-facing toggle.

3D browser farm-to-table island sim (Three.js): farm, cook, serve, reinvest, revive the island. Stylized toon look — 2–3 band cel ramp, beveled multi-part models, bright cool outdoors against a warm lamp-lit interior, toon water whose foam scales with boat speed; fill farm, island and restaurant to every orbit angle with structures and scatter. Camera: third-person perspective ~6m behind and above, 20° down, 360° yaw, pitch clamped -10° to -55°, smoothed follow retargeting to mount or boat, spring-arm pull-in on occlusion. Movement is camera-relative: A/D screen-left/right, W/S screen-forward/back, never inverted or swapped. One context key covers till/seed/water/harvest/feed/gather/repair/cook/serve, plus keys to ride or sail. Loop: till, seed and water plots, harvest at maturity before crops overripe; feed animals for timed milk/eggs/meat; ride or sail out to gather materials and repair sites, each repair unlocking a zone, seed, animal or recipe and raising footfall; cook recipes on a timer; serve dishes to seated customers before their ring countdown — correct serves pay money scaled by satisfaction, wrong or late ones cut it, and the closing tier sets next session's customer count; reinvest in upgrades, recipes and staff automation; save anytime. No win or lose state. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled, higher-segment custom silhouettes, keeping background props economical.

Browser first-person arena wave roguelite shooter in Three.js/WebGL2 with physics prop destruction, comic cel-shaded: thick depth-scaled black ink outlines on all geometry, 3-band quantized toon shading, no specular, doodle grunge overlay. Enclosed dark bowl arenas (magenta/deep-purple/dark-red base, hue rotating per arena) with tiered platform stacks, breakables, sweeping spotlights and fog-faded crowd stands. Warm gold-orange emissive only on interactive props, hazards and currency; cool cyan only for skill pulses; UI chrome fixed near-black-and-gold. Camera: first-person, FOV 78, eye ~1.7m, head-locked with no lag, free yaw, pitch clamped ±85°, never third-person; held emitter and clawed hands always visible in a near layer. Movement is camera-relative: A/D strafe to the visible screen sides at any yaw, W/S forward and back, never inverted or swapped. Controls: PointerLock look, hold LMB fire, RMB melee, Q throws cycled bombs, E grapple, Space jump/double-jump/glide/climb, CTRL air-stomp, LMB-hold grab and RMB kick props. Loop: equip persistent gear, then each seeded arena spawns a wave (bots_left) plus 3 optional challenges; kill with 3 separately-ammoed guns, melee, bombs and velocity-scaled thrown props while grappling, gliding and stomping (radial AoE plus shockwave ring); kills within a 3s window each add +0.5x to a wreck multiplier that scales cash and decays. bots_left at 0 settles cash and challenge bonuses, then a shop of 3 run-only upgrade cards (buy/reroll, infinite ammo) and a portal to a harder arena. Clearing arena 5 wins, HP 0 ends the run; unspent run cash becomes meta cash for permanent gear; restarting keeps meta, clears run upgrades.

Build Warlord's Ledger, a settlement-and-roster management RPG in an original broken realm: 2.5D as a true 3D Three.js scene, procedural low-poly, React HUD frame. Camera: locked orthographic oblique top-down, ~35° pitch, 45° yaw, no orbit/pan/zoom beyond brief jolts on combat resolution and build completion that return exactly to pose; clicks project onto that ground plane. Loop: click an adjacent node of a node+link world map to travel one day; each tick advances production, dispatch timers, and date-scheduled events/challengers. Facility grids spend Coin+Timber on timed builds raising Grain/Coin/Timber/Levy output and caps; recruit companions into a capped roster, dispatch idle ones 2–4 days for rewards, and send a party of four at challenger nodes, auto-resolved by comparing summed party Power to fixed enemy Power side by side — wins yield gear and resources; losses cost Levy and retreat the hero to the nearest owned settlement, and the run never ends. Research and daily-capped cultivation raise Power permanently; state persists. Rounded stone-and-timber keeps with beveled roofs and banners on instanced contour terrain, warm daylight, distant ridgelines, earth-gold UI framing the natural earth scene; never flat empty ground.

Build "Fault Lines," an original Three.js/WebGL2 narrative-choice RPG where dice-checked dialogue accumulates into branching endings. Camera: orthographic isometric, fixed near 45° azimuth / 30° pitch over the walkable area; no orbit, pan or zoom; only a <250ms dice-resolution shake returning to the exact pose. Controls: left-click paths the avatar to highlighted interaction points; Space advances lines; 1–4 pick options. Loop: spend 9 points across Body/Mind/Spirit (1–5) → explore, inspect clues, reach an NPC → portrait-flanked dialogue → 2–4 options tagged cooperate/question/lie/manipulate/befriend, sub-threshold ones greyed → a risk option rolls d20 + skill×2 once against 10/14/18 → outcome and tag pick the consequence branch and shift that NPC's trust/respect/hostility and global morality → met objectives unlock the next scene. Failed checks close paths, never end play; morality and key relationships select reconciliation, confrontation or betrayal, with progress persisted. A rusted offshore platform in cool daylight, then a dark back-kitchen under a warm spotlight cone, both rendered in graphic-novel style: thick uneven black outlines on depth/normal edges, blocky cel shading, desaturated earth tones; no empty planes or bare primitives.

Build an original solarpunk industrial-fantasy 3D combined-arms tactical RTS with Three.js: a wetland archipelago of ceramic armor, recycled steel, tidal shallows and translucent crystal glow. Camera: perspective strategy view, distance 18–52, full 360° yaw, pitch clamped 42–68° downward; WASD and edge scroll project onto camera-forward/right ground vectors so A/D move screen-left/right and W/S screen-forward/back at any yaw, Q/E rotate, the wheel zooms, and roofs or canopies hiding friendlies turn translucent. Orders: drag-box selection, right-click with attack outranking movement, and F1–F3 for the commander's recon pulse, smoke and inspire repair. Loop: deploy → scout through fog of war and patrols → fight with suppression and flanking → engineers capture relays for supply, garrison buildings and seize disabled vehicles while a workshop turns supply into smoke or repair packs → capture sets a checkpoint, then rain and fog cut vision, accuracy and off-road speed as two warned map-edge counterattack waves arrive → results award command points with checkpoint or full retry; losing the commander or every unit fails. Layer every view: reeds in front, roads, nodes and fighting midground, salt cliffs and mist islands behind; authored geometry with thickness and finished backs, long daylight shadows, rain fog deepening with distance without dulling friendly cyan outlines or objective markers. Chain two missions: seize a relay and hold the bridgehead, then escort a crystal core to extraction, persisting progress locally. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled or higher-segment custom geometry instead of box-only assembly, keeping background props economical if you do.

Build 'Ashbloom: Rite of the Verdant Dancer', a single-player 3D action-RPG farming life-sim in Three.js/WebGL2: cel-shaded toon surfaces with distance-scaled dark outlines, an Eastern pastoral region of timber hamlets, torii gates, tilled soil rows and cherry petals in bright daylight against desaturated cold-violet blight. Camera: third-person over-shoulder ~4.5m back, ~18° pitch-down, free yaw, pitch clamped -10° to -55°, ~0.15s damped follow, pull in to 2.2m on occlusion, half-body framing during bond dialogue. Controls: camera-relative WASD (screen left/right never inverts), Shift sprint, left-click 3-hit melee combo, right-hold charged bow, Q rite beam on a damage-filled gauge, Space dodge-roll with i-frames, Tab lock-on strafe, E to till/water/harvest/talk, B build. Loop: only the rite drains blight-node integrity, and a cleared node dissolves its thorns, brightens the land, drops a resource cache and opens tillable soil → till, plant, water and harvest crops over in-game days → spend crops and caches to raise village vitality and recruit residents → dialogue and gifts lift two NPCs to bond L2, enlisting one as a following, auto-attacking companion → deliver a resource set at the shrine to revive the dormant guardian for a region buff → defeat the 3-phase telegraphed region leader; days and season stages advance, crossfading tint, flora and crop viability. Enemies telegraph strikes; defeat respawns you at the settlement with resources intact, never a game-over. Blight violet marks hazards only, warm primaries mark player and allies, and neither tints UI text; fill the field with instanced props and plots, not empty planes.

Build a 2.5D side-scrolling run-and-gun platformer in Three.js/WebGL2: real 3D geometry played on one locked 2D plane — never flat 2D, never free orbit. Camera: perspective side view, slight downward pitch, horizontal follow on the centered player only, no rotation or zoom; impact shake returns to the exact locked pose. Controls: run, double-jump 5u gaps, climb ledges, 8-direction aim by holding a direction while firing, grenade, grapple, charged shot; optional two-player split-screen. Loop: pick one of three difficulties that shift HP and checkpoints → skippable cel-shaded comic interlude → traverse hazards and spiked hover drones → a rail-platform ride defending a cyan shield dome through three drone waves → a boss that swaps attack sets at 60% and 25% HP, exposing a glowing weak point after each burst and enraging in its last phase → next stage → ending. Bolt hits fill a segmented meter spent on a piercing charged shot; grenades are a counted AoE resource; the grapple yanks you to an anchor or a hazard to you, then cools down. Zero HP or a broken shield restarts at the last checkpoint. Stage three depths: foreground occluders, a bright readable midground play strip, dimmed desaturated parallax distance; brazier-amber temple and violet dune dusk with volumetric light shafts and drifting embers; the lone red dark-trimmed hero stays the most salient object.

Build a failure-free first-person low-poly walking sim in a dusk forest-farm meadow with Three.js. Camera: eye height 1.65 m, free yaw, pitch clamped −75°/+80°. Controls: WASD, mouse look, E; movement is camera-relative on the ground: A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted. Loop: roam one continuous plot; facing an animal or hidden glowing egg within 2.5 m raises a prompt; E opens original dialogue (movement locked) or collects the egg once, tallying talked/found counts; E at the stone rune arch triggers a white-out, a summary, then re-entry. Fixed dusk: warm key light, long soft shadows, orange-to-violet gradient sky, flat-shaded vertex colors, instanced trees and grass filling fore/mid/background in every direction; forest and warm fog block the edges. Optionally build one or two focal props (the arch, an animal) with richer beveled, higher-segment silhouettes rather than box assemblies, keeping background props economical.

Browser Three.js/WebGL detective adventure alternating a rain-slick neon-noir city with a cold-violet non-euclidean deduction labyrinth where the case's lies become traps. Cel-shaded outlined characters over a PBR wet-gloss world; a self-lit violet-cyan companion orb, the brightest local light, pulses near clues; exteriors carry rain, steam, neon signage and scatter inside an enclosing hazy skyline, never an empty plane. Camera: third-person follow ~2.2m up/5m back, pitch clamped -35..22deg, smoothed mouse look, pull in on obstruction, recenter after 2.5s idle. Controls: WASD camera-relative on XZ (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted or axis-swapped), E interact, Tab archive, Q/F switch/use ability, Shift dodge, Space slash. Loop: take the objective; inspect outlined nodes and question witnesses for one archived clue each, unlocking clue-gated dialogue; ECHO_SIGHT reveals ghost-residue clues, VEIL_STEP unlocks guarded testimony; the required clue set warps you in, conviction refilled to 3; traps telegraph 0.6s and cost 1 conviction, dodging grants i-frames, gates open only on the matching archived clue, wrong picks spawning a trap wave; at the truth core a phantom throws three false claims: pick counter-evidence within 12s and slash to break each round, errors costing conviction; the verdict names the culprit and unlocks the next case or ability. Conviction zero returns you to the labyrinth entry, clues kept. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled custom geometry instead of box-only assembly, keeping background props economical.

Build NEON VELOCITY: PULSE DRIFT, a browser first-person high-speed movement shooter in Three.js/WebGL2. Camera: first-person perspective, unlimited yaw, pitch clamped ±85°, weapon in its own near layer. Controls: camera-relative WASD on the horizontal plane (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted), LMB hitscan fire, Shift sprint burst, Space jump plus double-jump, Ctrl slide. Loop: spawn facing the arena, grab a weapon pickup, enter the zone to trigger enemy waves — self-detonating rushers forcing constant motion, ranged gunners holding high ground — shred them with overpowered guns (rifle, scatter cannon, beam; infinite ammo, brief overheat); kills in a 3s window stack a score multiplier, weak-point and airborne kills pay bonuses; clearing opens the exit portal. Hits drain a regenerating shield, then 3 lives; at zero the run ends and results show score, peak combo and high score with next-stage/retry/restart across 2–3 escalating, non-interchangeable stages. Look: near-black void arena of emissive neon magenta/cyan/green faceted slabs under a posterize + ordered-dither pass, speed-driven red/cyan radial aberration kept clean at the crosshair, bloom bursts on kills; symbol debris, distant silhouettes and one procedural sky dome fill fore/mid/background at every angle, never empty black; shake and aberration reducible to zero. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled, higher-segment custom geometry rather than box assembly, keeping background props economical.

Build Hollow Vigil in Three.js/WebGL: an unarmed player explores a place of confinement, scavenges drawers for key items that unlock gated areas, and hides from one relentless stalker across three chapters (woodland cemetery, hotel corridor, church). Camera alternates per chapter: first-person at 1.6m eye height, free yaw, pitch clamped ±70°, movement on camera forward/right; and a side camera locked ~6m out, facing fixed, planar movement, no rotation. A/D always move screen-left/right. Controls: WASD, Shift run, Ctrl crouch, E interact/pick up/enter or exit hiding, Tab inventory. Loop: search a room, unlock the next area, get detected by a 90°/10m vision cone plus gait-scaled hearing (lit targets seen 1.5x farther) as the stalker runs patrol→suspicious→chase→search, then break line of sight or dive under a bed or into a wardrobe where you are immobile and silent but can still be found; contact captures you and rolls back to the last checkpoint with items kept; reaching the final exit with its prerequisites met completes the escape. Crouching lowers visibility and noise. Visuals: near-black silhouettes with red fresnel rims, one handheld-lamp light pool, layered volumetric fog (sickly yellow-green outdoors, near-black indoors), and a fullscreen scanline/grain/aberration pass that intensifies with threat; red means danger only, and every view needs foreground clutter, midground landmarks like the bell tower, and fog-closed depth, never empty flat planes.

Build a 3D Three.js/WebGL browser game where a mischievous city bird wreaks cartoon chaos across three low-poly, flat-shaded, bright-daylight urban locales: a café district, a public beach, a residential backyard. Camera: perspective third-person follow ~6u behind and above at ~20° downward pitch, yaw damped to the bird's heading, pulling in on dive. Controls are camera-relative on the horizontal plane — A moves screen-left, D screen-right, never flipped: WASD fly, Space ascend/hover, Shift dash, C land, E grab, left-click dive/throw, F screech, R ultimate. Loop: dive-strikes topple pedestrians and props for points; screeches scatter nearby targets; a carried item slows you and throws on a parabolic arc for area destruction; chained hits raise a combo multiplier; eating glowing food charges energy until R fires a warm yellow-orange radial shockwave destroying everything within 8u. Canines grab only a landed bird while raptors chase in the air; a grab stuns and drops the item, costing time or score but never ending the run — dash or ascend out of range to escape. Hitting the count or score target activates an exit perch; reaching it settles score and unlocks scenes, creatures and upgrades; timer expiry fails the level; also an untimed free-roam mode. Every scene must show foreground, midground and background layers, large structures, dense instanced scatter and directional shadows — no empty planes.

A 2.5D browser management sim: a lone reclaimer clears and restores overgrown isometric ruins. Three.js/WebGL2 under a fixed orthographic isometric camera at ~35° downward — no orbit, zoom, or follow, only a brief impact shake that returns to the exact locked pose; panning stays in scene bounds, with map travel between unlocked locations. Click a target and the reclaimer walks to it. Loop: energy (cap 60, regen 1/90s) gates clearing — common obstacles cost 3–8 energy and leave drops plus buildable ground, sturdy ones need a stackable Charge tool selected first and consume one; harvest regrowing nodes, run production timers, fill board orders for coins, energy, or rare materials; invest materials to swap a damaged landmark to its restored mesh and unlock content; clearing every obstacle bordering a locked block opens it, and restoring the gateway landmark opens the second biome. Zero energy pauses the session but never ends it; progress persists. Fill the locked frame with a dense diorama of rounded beveled volumes framed by overhanging branches and rock lips, a readable midground interaction grid, and fog-bounded depths with no empty corners. Biome identity is color temperature — warm coastal daylight on saturated grass and rippling water-blue sea versus a dim cavern of breathing teal crystals; damaged surfaces desaturated, restored bright. Warm wood-brown capsule HUD at the edges; never flatten to 2D or free the camera.

Build Meadowhearth Homestead, a first-person 3D farm and commerce sim in Three.js/WebGL2, saved to localStorage.

Render low-poly hand-painted pastoral: faceted beveled procedural geometry, instanced grass, fences and trees, hemisphere fill plus a directional cascaded-shadow sun and a warm workshop point light, never a black frame. Keep fore/mid/far fill in every direction — soil ridges, barn/stall/workshop, village cluster and tree lines; no bare planes or billboards.

Camera: 70° FOV, eye height 1.7 m, free yaw, pitch clamped −60°..+75°, mouse look without inertia, no third-person switch or auto-recenter. Controls: camera-relative WASD on the ground plane (A screen-left, D screen-right, W forward, never axis-swapped), left click uses the held tool, E takes the crosshair action within 2.5 m with a warm-white Fresnel rim on focus, 1–6 hotbar.

Loop: buy seeds and livestock → till, sow, water daily, since skipped water pauses growth → harvest at zero due-days → feed animals for next-day milk, eggs or wool and pet them for affection bonuses → craft inputs into higher-value goods → sell from stall slots for money and XP → reinvest in slots, a greenhouse, and villager relationships that unlock better stock → sleep to settle growth, production and wages, as seasons shift plantable crops and light temperature. No failure state; an empty purse only limits buying.

Optionally, if water fills much of the view, use animated waves with Fresnel blending and wave-distorted real-time planar reflections, with a static environment map as fallback.

A 2.5D pixel bullet-heaven survivor roguelite road trip through biome-banded route nodes to a two-phase boss. Render a true 3D Three.js scene, not layered sprites: chunky beveled voxel-pixel units and props under even daylight with soft contact shadows, foreground wreck occluders, open midground arena, distant skyline band. Camera: orthographic oblique top-down high-angle, locked pose, following the player by translation only — no orbit, zoom, or projection change; brief hit shake snaps back. Controls: screen-relative WASD on the play plane, pointer aim bias, drag and R-rotate items. Loop: spend fuel on a route node → survive a 90s stop as edge spawns escalate and weapons auto-fire a piercing 5-shot fan at nearest enemies → kills drop XP orbs; each level-up airdrops one item → place multi-cell rotatable items on an 8×6 grid where orthogonal neighbors stack tagged bonuses and a workbench fuses two into a stronger one with a legendary roll, overflow blocking Confirm → the next band scales enemy HP, damage, spawns. Recruit nodes add roster survivors. Below 50% HP the boss adds summons and a radial slam; 0 HP ends the run. Keep combat brighter than the mid-dark ground: warm-glow player, pale enemies, white-hot-to-orange projectiles, cool cyan chain arcs, wood/parchment HUD never biome-tinted.

Build a browser 2.5D isometric puzzle-adventure in Three.js: a chibi seeker descends one-way through contrasting nostalgic era zones — warm terracotta mall, dim teal cinema — to recover a lost keepsake. Each zone is a painterly floating diorama: tiered platforms and stairs, foreground railings and signage filling every corner, distant era facades fading into blue-violet void, a warm key spotlight on the focal tier against cool ambient fill, soft shadows, no bare gaps, chibi figures dwarfed by finer sets. Camera: orthographic 3/4 downward and locked — no orbit, zoom, follow or pan, only a ≤250ms shake on unlock and boss defeat, returning to the exact pose. Controls: WASD/arrows or click-to-move on the ground plane, E on proximity-glowing hotspots, 1–4 inventory, H for a free companion hint. Loop: explore, gather items, set the zone's one gate puzzle to its target node state (illegal moves revert; undo/reset) to unlock the descent exit, optionally give an item to one NPC, then the exit-blocking boss, beatable only in the arcade cabinet's minigame — a separate 2D pixel canvas layer with CRT scanlines whose tile-grid move/attack/guard win writes back his defeat. No overworld death; a minigame loss retries endlessly. The deepest zone recovers the keepsake and ends the run.

Build a Three.js/WebGL first-person arena shooter in a compact cover-dense masonry ruin under cold overcast daylight; any registered hit kills instantly. Camera: FOV 75, ~1.6m eye height, PointerLock look, pitch clamped ±85°, never third-person. Controls: WASD projected on camera-forward/right so screen left/right never inverts; LMB fire, R reload, V cycles SEMI/BURST/AUTO. Loop: pick Team Deathmatch, Domination or Free-For-All, then 1 of 3 loadouts differing in fire rate, magazine and range; crosshair hitscan kills the first actor in range unless cover blocks it; an empty magazine blocks fire until a timed reload from finite reserve. Bots hold cover lanes and engage on sight; death costs a short protected respawn far from enemies; score cap or timer ends the match on a scoreboard. In Domination, standing alone on the central point flips ownership and ticks score. Layer a beveled viewmodel and forearm over arches, low walls and instanced rubble against a ruin silhouette; no flat planes or bare primitives.

2D GBC-pixel cute-fantasy hybrid of top-down shooting and side-view platforming, camera scrolling with the player. Tap shoots; hold charges mana-fueled magic, degrading to a plain shot when empty. Zero hearts fails a stage; stars buy upgrades, and clearing three opens the final boss.

Cozy 2.5D kitchen-hut serving sim as a real Three.js scene: soft-beveled low-poly diorama of cream walls, teal wainscot, checker floor, and chibi animal patrons at a right-side street window. Camera: fixed close-up on the cook station, ~25° downtilt, order ticket top-right; no orbit/pan/zoom, only a ≤6px shake on serve or burn that snaps back. Controls: mouse click/drag ingredients. Loop: a bell brings a patron whose ticket shows an ordered 2–5 layer stack and a countdown → heat items raw→done→overcooked→charred (voided, refetch), shaders carrying doneness → stack in exact order → serve; stars from layer match plus time left, tips buying upgrades. Timeout scores zero and the patron leaves; no game over, save anytime. Arrival pace: frenetic, relaxed, or focus-timer.

2.5D physics slingshot puzzle in Three.js: a true 3D matte-clay scene of beveled volumes and soft shadows, with all motion locked to one vertical plane. Camera: fixed oblique overhead-side view framing the left launcher through the right structure zone, no orbit or zoom beyond a brief impact shake that snaps back. Drag the fixed Y-shaped elastic launcher for angle and power with a dotted parabola preview, release to fire, and tap Space mid-flight to dash the yellow projectile. Each level spends an ordered queue of rounded creature projectiles — red heavy-impact, yellow dasher, patterned area burst — arcing into stacked stone, wood and brick that topple and crush the green targets beneath. Clear all targets to win with 1–3 stars and unlock the next level; an exhausted queue with targets alive means retry. Dress foreground, midground and corners rather than leaving a bare plane.

2D side-view base defense: auto-firing cyan-green towers hold a dusk horizon over mirror water against magenta flora. Craft underground, deploy, survive day waves; the avatar only repositions and repairs. Breach or zero hearts ends a run; unlocks persist toward a Beacon win. Optional generated avatar sprite sheet; if used it must be the default rendering, procedural art an internal failure fallback, not a player toggle.

2.5D Three.js: hand-drawn doodle dioramas — thick uneven black contours, flat saturated fills, paper grain — for a comic first day at a whimsical workshop. Warm cream narrative sets hard-cut to one dominant puzzle hue: crimson void, forest green, console yellow. Camera: locked, no orbit/pan/zoom; orthographic 35° three-quarter over the isometric puzzle, front-facing for dialogue and console; only a 150–250ms shake returning to the exact pose. Controls: clicks, plus direction pads projected onto the iso plane so movement matches the view. Loop: advance dialogue, picking tone-tagged replies (warm/witty/blunt) that store counters and vary NPC reactions; narrative gates three retryable puzzles — a console whose sticky-note rule resolves to the one slot clearing its red alerts, and an iso grid stepped tile by tile where pillars block and stepping off resets to start; then lock one component per group; the reveal assembles the output from those parts and tones, ending with a hidden-gem tally and replay. Dress all four corners; no flat planes.

Three.js first-person shooter in a sunbaked frontier of PBR weathered wood, adobe and brass: a rutted street funneling to a mesa skyline, then a narrow rail-car corridor, with enemies as high-contrast camera-facing bold-ink billboard sprites. Camera: first-person at ~1.7m eye height, weapon viewmodel centered-lower, pitch clamped ±80°. Controls: WASD is camera-relative (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted), mouse looks, LMB fires hitscan, RMB narrows FOV to aim, R reloads. Loop: advance the lane, trigger hostiles, drop sprites with 2× headshots, grab ammo/health/keys, clear the zone, unlock the gated door, then a comic-ink interlude into the rail-car level. Four guns differ in viewmodel, rate, magazine and reload; death resumes at the last checkpoint. Long sun shadows, drifting dust and an engraved brass HUD bar ground it, plus a bot deathmatch.

Build a browser first-person roguelite arena shooter in Three.js: pick FFA or Survival plus one of three classes (dash ranger, slow-shot bulwark, drain tinker). Camera: first-person, FOV 78°, free yaw, pitch clamped ±85°, no third-person pullback or roll. Controls: WASD, Space jump, PointerLock look, LMB fire, Shift/E/Q abilities; movement is camera-relative on the XZ plane with A/D exactly screen-left/right and W/S forward/back, never inverted or axis-swapped. Loop: pick 1 of 4 cards in 12s (timeout takes the first) → fight 3–5 cover-strafing bots with visibly traveling projectiles, floating damage numbers, headshot multipliers and high time-to-kill, abilities spending regenerating Energy on cooldown while Health never regenerates → draft again so upgrades stack into a build → at the round cap rank by kills or survival points, then replay. One enclosed blocky low-poly arena of flat high-saturation hue-coded blocks (green and red walls, orange floor, blue and purple accents), chest-high cover, pillars, platforms, launching jump-pads and explosive barrels; bright ambient plus one soft key, contact shadows only; crosshair above green Health and cyan Energy bars. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled, higher-segment or custom geometry rather than box-only assembly, keeping background props economical.

Browser Three.js/WebGL low-poly traveling-merchant trade game: bright saturated fairytale daylight, faceted cottages with painted roofs, swaying canopies. Camera: movable third-person orbit behind the merchant, ~25° down, 6–9 units, pulling in near buildings. Controls: camera-relative WASD with unswapped axes (A screen-left, D screen-right), drag to orbit, E to interact, M for the map. Loop: start with 250 coins and a 6-slot pack; buy cheap at vendor stalls, where three towns price six goods in brown/silver/gold value tiers, leaving a cross-town spread; slots cap what you carry; higher-tier trades open a haggle with accept, reject, or one counter; pay a map fee to travel, which switches town and refreshes prices; sell high and reinvest in pack, route-reveal and haggle upgrades until a wealth threshold ends the run in a settlement with restart. Interactables rim-glow in range; every reachable angle shows foreground props, midground stalls and vendors, roofs, walls and hills closing the horizon, never bare void. Optionally, one or two identity-critical focal props may use richer beveled or higher-segment geometry instead of box-only assembly, if background props stay economical.

Three.js/WebGL2 2.5D gothic sidescroller: a near-white glowing rider on a skeletal steed crosses a monochrome hand-drawn funerary world where an ending becomes a beginning. Camera: fixed side-view perspective, horizontal follow only, ground receding right into depth. Controls: hold Right/D/mouse to ride forward with easing, release to slow — the only verb, no failure. Loop: graveyard moor → tangled woods → cliff edge in fixed order, exit markers fading to black, position-fired beats swelling glow and music; the terminus auto-plays a horizon-glow climax, then the rider dissolves into light with Replay. Grayscale ink and dry-brush surfaces, near-black instanced tombstones and dead trees framing the corners, bloom only on brightest extremes.

Strict 2D fixed-camera idle game: a tamer auto-runs right, auto-battles by a six-element ring, captures on KO, and earns badges toward a Champion and prestige with no input. Bright daytime parallax, outlined pixel sprites on one ground line. Optionally use a generated tamer sprite sheet; if adopted, it is the default visible rendering, procedural art only an internal fallback, never a player-facing skin.

Build Sunspire Gauntlet, a browser 3D third-person trap-gauntlet action-platformer in Three.js/WebGL2: an agile ranged adventurer crosses lethal timed hazards through levels alternating a bright domed sandstone desert city and an oppressive torchlit brick dungeon. Camera: over-shoulder perspective behind and just above the player, mouse-movable; never invert screen left/right, no first-person or top-down. Controls: camera-relative WASD (A screen-left, D screen-right, W forward), Space jump, Shift dodge roll with i-frames, RMB aim + LMB fire, F melee, E interact. Loop: time hazards (fire pits kill on contact but clear in one jump; spike columns extend on a 1.5s cycle leaving a 0.7s safe retracted window, telegraphed by a 0.5s flare), solve a switch/align/shoot-distant-target puzzle that opens a gate or disables a hazard segment, defeat path-blocking skeletons, pass a checkpoint storing respawn and refilling HP, then reach the exit portal to advance; final clear reports time and deaths. Death is frequent but fair: HP 0 or hazard contact respawns at the last checkpoint, that segment reset. Keep scenes densely layered — foreground scatter, midground platforms and hazards, background domes, spires or a torchlit vanishing point — PBR sandstone, gold, glazed teal tile and brick on instanced kits, warm sun outdoors versus torch point-lights and warm depth fog indoors, and hot red-orange reserved for lethal hazards so player, skeletons and traps stay separable by value. No bare empty planes.

Two-player same-screen arena duel in Three.js/WebGL: low-poly chibi duelists on a floating grid of beveled tiles over a lethal emissive lava/water underlayer, inside a bright sky dome ringed by desaturated skyline/castle/forest silhouettes, no void at any angle. Camera: split the viewport into two equal side-by-side scissor/viewport halves, each a perspective camera trailing behind-and-above its own avatar at ~35° downward tilt, no free orbit or opponent-view cuts. Controls: WASD or left stick moves along camera-forward/right on the tile plane (A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted or swapped); mouse or stick aims, click or space lobs. Loop: a stepped tile tints as warning then collapses 1.2s later into an irreversible hole; a lobbed arced explosive destroys a 3×3 cluster on impact behind a 3s ring cooldown; tiles never return, so the shrinking floor forces confrontation until an avatar loses all footing and falls into the hazard—last survivor wins, simultaneous falls draw, rematch rebuilds a fresh arena. Optionally, if hazard water fills much of the view, use animated waves, Fresnel blending, and wave-distorted real-time planar reflections, with a static environment map as fallback.

Fixed-camera 2D pixel side-view lane: regenerating mana deploys four countering classes that march right; kills pop two-choice level-ups, razing the enemy tower wakes a boss, your tower falling loses. Optional generated sprite sheet; if adopted it is the default visible character art, procedural art only an internal failure fallback, never a player-facing toggle.

Fixed-camera 2D with limited drops: aim the top drop point so a squishy blob bounces off pegs into faced orbs, growing heavier and bouncing lower; clear all to win, stars buy shop boosts. Optional generated blob sprite sheet, if adopted the default rendering; procedural only an internal failure fallback, never a player-facing toggle.

2D point-and-click RPG in fixed hand-painted screens: click to walk and inspect; a Strength/Agility/Intelligence lean gates puzzles and dialog; side-view turn-based duels; choices resolve one of three endings. Optional generated hero sprite sheet; if adopted it must be the default visible rendering, with procedural art only an internal fallback, never player-facing.

First-person fetch-and-place puzzle in Three.js: across a flat-shaded low-poly sunny lakeside grove of gazebos, dock and conifer ring, carry 8 objects into matching green ghost slots. Camera: pointer-locked, eye height 1.7 m, never third-person; WASD moves camera-relative on the ground inside barriers. Loop: crosshair an item, left-click to hold it translucent below the sightline, snap it into its bound slot within 1.5 m with a cyan burst; wrong items never snap, and right-click returns one to spawn, resetting the combo. At 8/8 the count-up timer stops and results total base, combo and speed bonuses into a local leaderboard, then replay resets. Green marks only slots, cyan only success; no 360° view is empty, and lake and foliage keep moving. Optionally the lake uses animated waves, Fresnel blending and wave-distorted real-time planar reflections; if adopted, a static environment map stays the fallback.

Build "Glyphlight Depths", a browser first-person voxel dungeon magic-shooter in Three.js: explore a 5-6 room maze of corridors and dead-end branches. Camera: pointer-locked, free yaw, pitch clamped ±70°, pushed out of walls so the void never shows. Controls: WASD along camera-forward/right projected onto the ground plane so A goes screen-left, mouse aims a fixed center crosshair, left-click casts. Loop: explore; enemies and traps wake as you approach; bolts fire every 0.35s for 15 of 100 mana that regenerates when you stop; time passage between cycling floor spikes and sustained flame jets; relics auto-collect within 2 units, raising collected/6; all six with health left wins, zero health loses, restart rebuilds the layout. Deep cool near-black brick with brighter grout, grey perspective tile floor, few warm braziers, exponential fog swallowing distance into black; three enemy types and amber relics are flat matte camera-facing billboards, the only saturated color, over warm health and cool mana bars. Optionally give one or two focal props beveled custom geometry instead of boxes, keeping background props economical.

Build Hollow Bastion Protocol, a browser top-down arena wave-survival shooter in a true 3D Three.js scene (no sprites, no 2.5D): a faceted low-poly war-mech fights crystalline drones in a bounded arena of beveled stone/ice floor, carved walls, broken pillars and edge portals under drifting per-stage fog, cool ambient and one directional key casting floor shadows — never a bare plane. Camera: perspective pitched ~60° down, ~22 units above and behind the hull, yaw/pitch/zoom locked, damped follow clamped inside the walls. Controls: WASD/arrows move screen-relative with horizontal and depth on separate axes (up = away, right = right, never inverted); cursor aims; hold LMB to fire; Space/RMB triggers the signature active on cooldown. Loop: pick 1 of 3 mechs → drones spawn from portals → kills drop XP orbs that level you up → the wave ends on clear or a 25s timer → draft 1 of 3 weapon/skill/trait cards, optionally socketing a gem → each wave raises count and tier → the final wave spawns a two-phase boss with telegraphed slams and radial shots, faster past 50% HP → stage grade, next stage retinted, three stages to victory. Physical, elemental and force damage keep fixed hues (steel white, cyan, magenta) and apply 0.5×/1×/1.5× resistances. HP 0 ends the run; restart resets build and level.

Third-person 3D island farm-and-restaurant life sim in Three.js/WebGL. Camera: ~6m behind the avatar, 20° downward pitch, 360° yaw orbit, pitch clamped 5–60°, lerped follow, blending to a fixed rig inside the restaurant. Controls: camera-relative WASD on the ground plane (A moves screen-left, D screen-right; axes never inverted or swapped), drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, E as the contextual verb for till/plant/harvest/feed/fish/cook/serve/repair, F mounts a ridable animal. Loop: till, plant, water to speed growth, and harvest crops at their Ready label; feed penned animals for products; fish and pick via a timing-bar minigame that just retries on a miss; cook recipes on a prep timer; serve seated customers before a 45s countdown ring empties for coins scaled 0.5×–1.5× by remaining time, a miss forfeiting only that payout; reinvest coins and materials into plots, recipe unlocks, and repairs of derelict sites that each reveal a new region with new seeds, animals and customers. Auto-save, no game-over. Render a dense beveled low-poly island: saturated grass-green and sky-blue outdoors, warm wood-and-cream interior, instanced trees, fences and crop rows amid windmill, waterfall and harbor filling every orbit angle; stylized water ripples harder while fishing, and a warm-gold fresnel rim pulses only on ripe crops.

First-person 3D mystery-exploration in a near-empty rustic folk village; Three.js/WebGL2, photoreal PBR timber, thatch, clay and mossy stone under warm ember firelight against a cool sky. Camera: perspective, eye height 1.7m, spawn at the village entry facing the burned hearths, pitch clamped ±80°, sway only on time-shifts and puzzle solves; never third-person, orbit or top-down. Controls: screen-relative WASD on the ground plane (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted or axis-swapped); a crosshair ray within 2.5m adds a warm rim glow and a line-glyph action label; E or click inspects, drag rotates and wheel zooms the object against a blurred backdrop, Tab journals, F shifts time at an anchor. Loop: roam, inspect a prop, log a clue fragment, combine fragments into an environmental puzzle action (wrong attempts revert with a hint, unlimited retries), then at a time-anchor pick a season so the world rebuilds dressing, light and colour temperature at your preserved position; alter the past, return later, and consequences propagate to unlock regions and fragments until the final fragment set plus a closing interaction resolves the story. No death; soft dead-ends resolve by finding more clues. Reserve peak orange-gold emission for the ember spirit, hearths and anchors, keep the HUD panel-free line work, and layer the held carved staff, cottages, fences and scatter into an enclosing treeline and hills — never bare planes. Optionally give one or two identity-critical focal props richer beveled or higher-segment custom geometry; if adopted, keep background props economical.

Build a first-person 3D browser battle royale where rounded plush toys fight to be last standing on a child's bedroom carpet. Three.js/WebGL2 with PointerLockControls, FOV 75, camera at the plush's head; yaw unlimited, pitch clamped ±80°, never third-person. Controls: WASD on camera-relative axes (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted or axis-swapped), Space jumps, gaps ≤3 units crossable; keys 1–5 or wheel instantly swap five weapons — hitscan auto rifle, spread shotgun, thrown bomb, knockback melee, fists. Loop: lobby (hat/cape/color, Practice or Royale, saved locally) → load 8 AI plushes → scatter spawn → fight from 100 HP → at 45 s then every 20 s an outer ring of carpet tiles collapses, dealing damage and fatal falls while squeezing survivors inward → last standing wins → results with placement and replay. Royale death is final; Practice respawns after 3 s. A red vignette pulses on hits and breathes below 30 HP; collapsing tiles glow along an advancing orange-red dissolve edge. Fill the room: block fortresses, toy boxes, dice and crayons, distant bookshelf silhouettes, bright daylight with soft shadows, hand-painted matte plush and beveled blocks, never bare primitives on a flat plane.

Strict 2D, camera panning vertically only: steer a hook from bright shallows into near-black depth where the bait halo shrinks and rare species hide. Dwell on the tinted target, dodge the rest, then hold left/right to keep the tension pointer in its safe band until reeled in. Ask up to two questions, judge good or evil from a trait handbook, then ascend or release; wrong ascends distort and cost a power. Collect 12 species.

Third-person 3D storybook game, fixed 16:9 canvas: a teal otter courier does chores in a miniature canal town of rounded, thick-walled cottages, docks, bridges and a windmill on calm blue-green water. Dress scenes densely: no blank ground or visible world edges. Camera: orbit follow-cam behind and above, full yaw, clamped pitch; blockers fade, never clip. Controls: camera-relative WASD (A screen-left, D screen-right, W forward), never inverted or swapped; Shift sprint, F interact, no jump. Loop: take one request at a time from a resident or notice tree, follow the coral beacon to the task zone, do a short gather/sort/carry-one-item/wipe/water/repair chore, then earn Community Glow as a leaf-green-to-gold pulse permanently restores that spot. Glow totals unlock Garden Dock, Laundry Lane, Market Boardwalk, Rooftop Greenhouse and the lit Celebration Pier finale in order. Nonviolent, no defeat: canal falls return you to the last safe point, nothing lost.

First-person voxel sandbox, Three.js on WebGL2: one persistent unit-cube world, no fail state. Camera: eye height 1.6, pointer-lock look, pitch clamped ±89°. Controls: WASD camera-relative on the horizontal plane (A screen-left, D screen-right, never inverted), Space jumps enough to mount one cube but not two. Loop: a centered-reticle raycast wireframe-previews the aimed cell, then the primary action places the active block in the adjacent empty cell or deletes the aimed solid one — never the base floor — and new cubes become standable; a toggle swaps place/remove, six block types, spawnable humanoids (max 8) idle and wander, and save/load restores edited cells, figures and camera pose exactly. Calm earthy daylight: beveled cubes with flat procedural face textures, translucent rippling water, sun shadows and top>side>underside luminance, and a gradient sky dome whose toggleable fog dissolves far cubes into a bright horizon band over terrain ringed by border hills.

Three.js WebGL2 tile-clear puzzle on a dressed tabletop: thick paperboard tiles, each class a hue plus a unique raised relief motif, seated in a rimmed matte-wood tray under a warm key light. Camera: one locked high three-quarter near-top-down view — never orbit, zoom or shake. Pointer only: hover outlines the orthogonally connected same-class group; click clears 3+ for n²×10 and spends one move. Loop: survivors fall straight down, refill enters from the far feeder lip, auto-formed groups resolve as waves with a rising multiplier, and a 6+ clear leaves an arrow tile clearing its line. Objectives against a move budget decide clear or fail; deadlock reshuffles rather than locks. No timer.

Flat 2D side view: a charm courier runs four hazard trials; one key strikes an enemy in reach, else dashes — no jump. Pressure rises by subtracting scenery detail; each ends in a camera-locked rival duel, the rival open only in telegraph recovery. Optional generated courier sprite sheet; if adopted it is the default player rendering, procedural art an internal failure-only fallback, never a skin or toggle.

Third-person 3D narrative exploration in Three.js/WebGL2: walk a warm alpine lake village where beveled voxel characters inhabit a hand-painted realistic low-poly world of turquoise water, timber-plaster houses, a leaning stone spire, pines and fog-layered ridges.

Camera: third-person, ~5.5m rear-upper, 22° downward pitch, 360° drag yaw, damped follow, spherecasting shorter near walls instead of clipping. Movement is camera-relative: A screen-left, D screen-right, W forward, S back, never inverted or axis-swapped. Controls: WASD, E interacts within 2m, J journal, Space advances dialogue, Esc closes views.

Loop: at a present-day lakeside overlook, approaching the hooded figure at the water triggers a submersion warp into the past village; explore and talk while collecting 6 lore sheets and 3 painterly artworks viewed fullscreen on dark; a timing or pattern minigame gates each of 3 story beats, with free retry and Skip after 3 fails; cleared beats dissolve region barriers, and all three trigger the climax flood — a rising water-level uniform on the Gerstner lake shader submerging the spire — then an ending tallying collection.

Dialogue choices commit irreversibly, setting per-NPC warm/neutral/guarded flags that gate later lines and color the ending; no lose state. Lake may add Fresnel and wave-distorted planar reflections.

2D pixel side-scroller: run and hold jump to wing-glide over instant-death lava while auto-firing pulses that shatter enemies. Blood coins unlock new guns at statue hubs; each stage ends with a two-phase boss. Dark caves, amber sky, neon-green platform edges.

Build a browser 3D near-isometric action loot-grind RPG in Three.js/WebGL: a lone blade-bearer grows a classical eastern stone-and-wood homestead into peak power. Camera: perspective ~45° pitch, yaw and pitch locked, following the hero by translation only (lerp 0.12, no orbit or zoom). Controls: WASD or click-to-move, camera-relative — A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted or swapped; left mouse attacks, Q/W/1–5 skills with windup and cooldown, E interacts, I bag, F food. Loop: at home grow crops, fish, tend livestock, cook ingredients into buff food; fight through a ruined settlement where enemies patrol, aggro, chase, show red overhead bars and drop white/blue/purple loot; mine an enemy-free cavern where ore nodes take several tool hits before yielding upgrade materials; beat the region boss for guaranteed rare-or-better gear and one recruitable offline ally; upgrade gear across three slots, level up, then sleep at the home bed — the only reset — advancing the day, respawning enemies and chests, growing crops one step, endlessly. HP0 downs the hero: respawn home, field progress lost, stored inventory kept. The companion auto-follows, auto-attacks, and boosts gather and mine rates. Keep every scene enclosed and densely propped in three depth layers, no bare primitives, lit by one shadowed directional key plus warm lantern points: cozy amber interiors against cold cyan-grey fogged dungeon and mine, tier-colored fresnel loot glow, red boss aura, gunmetal UI with neutral text and amber only on currency numerals.
Flat 2D puzzle: rotate the level 90° left/right, camera fixed, so gravity drops a green grid body onto a star in fewest moves; undo. Ivory slab, gray walls, saturated background.

Build a Three.js/WebGL2 browser 3D open-city taxi sim: drive an amber taxi through one seamless coastal district of sand-beige Mediterranean mid-rises, palm boulevards and marina waterfront under one day-azure/dusk-warm sun rig with soft shadows, fog, wet-asphalt and speed-blur shaders. Camera: FOV 60 chase 6.5m back, 3.2m high, pitch −12°, yaw easing to heading, springing to 3.0m to avoid clipping; C toggles a first-person interior with cyan gauges. Controls: A/D steer relative to vehicle heading, never inverted (A is screen-left), W throttle, S brake/reverse, F accept/confirm, hold Tab for an 8-way radial. Loop: cruise until a beacon fare pin accepts on a full stop within 20m → follow the A* road-graph route → satisfaction falls on collisions, harsh braking, speeding and red lights (fines settle later) and rises when radial-answered passenger requests land in time → road events block a segment and auto-reroute, control retained → park to settle fare, tip and 1–5 stars from satisfaction, plus xp. Between fares refuel, repair, upgrade, hire drivers, unlock skills; state saves locally. Wet weather darkens asphalt, lengthens braking and skids. A crash, zero satisfaction or an empty tank voids only that fare; no game over. Fill every reachable view with instanced traffic, pedestrians, palms and props, never empty planes; orange stays route/accent, amber entity-only. Marina water may use animated waves with Fresnel reflections.

2D top-down watercolor tearoom sim: repair derelict floor, place tables and a kitchen, assign staff, set prices, then open a timed day where customers seat, order, eat, and pay.
