Coins/Renown/Sprigs gate recipes and one back-room expansion; strays raised to adoption grant passive bonuses. Camera pans and zooms in-plane; insolvency is forgiven, not fatal.

Strict 2D vertical pinball ascent: flip left/right paddles (keys or screen halves) to knock a magenta mote up through procedural crystal-then-ashen chambers as an amber flood rises. Bumpers and spinners deflect it; gems buy a keeper's shortcut. Camera tracks the apex, never lower. A fall below the paddles or flood contact is fatal.

Frostpaw Downhill Rush: a Three.js arcade downhill ski racer in low-resolution pixelated 3D — a cartoon snow creature carves procedural slopes walled by teal conifers, past blue ice ramps, red rings and yellow flags, fog closing the distant ridge. Layer foreground, midground and background; no empty unlit plane.
Camera: follow 6u behind, 3u above, 18° tilt, 60° FOV, yaw locked to the racer's heading with no free orbit, recentering 0.4s after steering stops, raycasting inward, FOV pulsing and pulling back at high multiplier.
Controls: A/D steer camera-relative onto the slope so screen-left never inverts; W throttles above gravity, S/Space brakes and carves, Space jumps ramps and rings.
Loop: pick one of three racers with distinct TURN/BOOST/WEIGHT/TRICK, descend as ramps, rings, flags and clean lines raise an uncapped +0.25 multiplier scaling top speed and speed-line density, while braking pauses it and a bench, rail or bush hit cuts 40% speed, tumbles 0.6s and resets it to 1.0. Race 3 AI for ranks 1–4, or time-trial a seeded track for a stored best; finishing or timing out ends in results whose restart regenerates the slope.

Browser third-person 3D toon-shaded turn-based party JRPG (Three.js), one self-contained chapter.

Camera: spring-arm follow behind the leader (~6.5 back, ~2.8 up, pitch −18°, clamped [−32,12]), tightening near walls without clipping; battle orbits the arena, dialogue uses shot-reverse-shot cuts. Controls: camera-relative WASD on the ground plane — A/D screen-left/right, W/S forward/back, never inverted or axis-swapped — mouse yaw+pitch, E interact, F cycles 1×/2×/4× speed, R toggles interruptible auto-battle.

Loop: title/save select → scripted scene → explore a town hub and field region, taking quests among patrolling enemies → contact starts battle, rear contact grants the party the first turn while a rear ambush reverses it → an AGI timeline orders Attack/Skill/Finisher/Guard/Retreat; SP pays skills, ZP charges on damage dealt and taken and spends at 100 on a burst finisher, a full Link gauge auto-fires a follow-up from a living adjacent ally → victory pays EXP, gold, drops and 30% HP → equip/skill/quest management unlocks the next region node → a two-phase boss hardening at 50% HP → chapter result; a wipe offers reload or restart.

Render a 3-band toon ramp with cyan rim light (downed units desaturate), stylized figures over realistically lit stone, wood and foliage, warm orange-to-pink additive finisher ribbons with bloom, god-ray shafts and region-tinted fog. Layer foreground arches, a midground plaza with props and NPCs, background rooftops and ridge under a sky dome, and a dusk-blue runic arena; no bare planes at any yaw. Body text stays neutral near-white, never environment- or VFX-tinted.

2D point-and-click adventure: a lantern-keeper searches fixed-frame hand-painted dusk-marsh scenes for a lost sibling. Click ground to walk, gold-outlined hotspots to look/take/use/talk, combine items to unlock exits. Two choices decide reunion or loss.

Three.js/WebGL2 open-water sandbox: pilot four physically distinct vessels in one calm daylight bay; no objective or fail state. Camera: right-drag orbit (free yaw, pitch -60° to +12°), scroll zoom 6–40 units, C eases chase → high-orbit → deck. Movement is camera-relative on the water plane: W/S throttle, A/D rudder, and A always swings the hull screen-left at any orbit angle. Loop: thrust ramps to a per-vessel top speed, drag decays it, yaw rate scales with speed so heading lags and the hull drifts; wake foam, bow spray and roll-tilt scale with speed and turn sharpness; one GLSL swell drives surface and hull bob; hulls soft-bounce off docks and rocks; a boundary current keeps them in the bay. V/1–4 switch vessels, the rest keeping momentum; R respawns all. Warm sun on cool #2E5A6E water, near-white contact foam, buoys, a rocky islet and a lighthouse headland, so no view reads as empty water.

Calm 2D dress-up studio: tap tabs to swap layered garments on a fixed front-facing figure; a dress clears tops and bottoms; per-character looks persist, finalized into a confetti showcase over a blurred party backdrop.

Real-time 3D war-strategy in Three.js: two asymmetric factions contest a fractured floating plateau of plates over a cloud-filled chasm. Camera: fixed ~55° oblique overhead perspective, no rotation; left-drag on empty terrain pans, drag delta mapped to world XZ and never inverted; wheel dollies between clamped tactical and overview distances; pressing a piece enters drag-place and suppresses panning. Loop: pick a faction (Bloomkin heal occupants; Cinder hit harder on contested frontiers), place a production structure on your foothold, resources accrue per owned plate, queue units, drag them onto adjacent neutral plates to claim or onto enemy plates to contest, where each tick the greater committed strength plus a defender bonus takes ownership. Hold 2 of 3 rift-anchor obelisks for a duration to win; losing all production is defeat. Terrain is matte low-saturation stone; teal and amber appear only on pieces and per-plate ownership overlays, white-hot contested seams, and anchor cores tinted to their controller. Fixed key light, instanced scatter per plate, distant islets and clouds, never a flat empty plane. Focal props may use richer beveled geometry.

Fixed side-on 2D twilight canyon: drag back on the hooded warden to set angle and power at once, firing a gravity-arced bolt. Modes: mesa target, drifting beacon, two-player duel. Keep the bolt brightest onscreen.

2D side view, one button: hold to thrust a coral glider up a deepening blue sky, scoring above a green line, then land on the amber pad. Higher peak narrows the safe window and survivable impact speed; a crash discards it. Camera pans vertically only.

Rimline Rally, a Three.js fixed-camera catch game: drag a cool teal hoop along one lane to intercept warm orange balls arcing down. Camera: locked perspective at (0,3.2,7.5) looking at (0,0.8,0), never orbiting or panning, only a damped miss shake returning to that pose. Controls: pointer drag raycasts onto the play plane to set hoop X, clamped to lane ends. Loop: spawn, eased arc, catch only when the ball center enters the band above the hoop mouth and overlaps it horizontally, score × multiplier (x2 at 3, x3 at 6, x4 at 10+), then the next ball falls faster. One miss ends the run; results show peak combo and best. Muted arena, warm key light, layered depth.
Flat 2D paper-doll dress-up: two figures on a fixed frontal stage before a soft evening backdrop. Click one to activate, click items to swap its clothes, shoes and hair layers; finalize the pair.

Build an original tabletop flick-football game in Three.js/WebGL2: a matte felt pitch with painted markings, rounded weighted figurines, a paneled ball, metal goals with soft nets, a dim wooden surround under a warm lamp. Camera: fixed elevated three-quarter pose framing both goals — no orbit, pan, zoom or follow, only a brief goal shake returning exactly to that pose. Controls: single pointer; hold an owned figure to aim along the pointer raycast onto the pitch plane, drag for clamped power previewed on the felt, release to flick, move off to cancel. Loop: one flick per turn; figures move the ball only by contact; a custom friction-and-rebound sim settles; a goal counts only when the ball fully crosses the line inside the frame; possession then alternates. A short turn limit ends the match; win 3 escalating AI matches for the cup. Team hue tints only figurines; focal props may use richer beveled geometry.
Fixed-frame illustrated 2D prep game: snap decor into room zones, stack up to 4 translucent drink layers that reblend live, then layer garments on a figure, ending in a showcase. No fail state.

2D paper-doll: tap swatches to swap face, hair, outfit, accessory layers on a front-facing figure across four stages, then Reveal. Hair color tints hair layers only. No fail state; calm aqua reef salon.
Fixed side-view 2D cel-shaded boulevard, click-only: tap passersby whose clothing marks tip tier, save 120 for a market stall, then stock and sell goods on margin and upgrade. No fail state.

Ramforge Rally: an original Three.js/WebGL2 combat kart racer — one heavy reinforced racer versus four AI rivals over two laps of an arid circuit.

Camera: chase rig ~7.5 back and 3.2 up, pitch clamped -16° to -8°, ~0.12s position smoothing with slower yaw catch-up so the road ahead stays framed; never top-down, inverted, or free-look.

Controls: arrows drive and steer, F uses the held power-up, Space fires the skill; steering is heading-relative, so left input always turns visibly left.

Loop: locked 3-2-1-GO, then throttle under a grip cap that breaks into controllable drifts; ram rivals — ram-mass momentum transfer along the contact normal shoves and slows the target and costs the attacker speed, unless a shield pops; drive over nodes for one held power-up — boost, shield, or a rival-slowing forward wave; rams and clean corners charge a meter that fires a per-vehicle signature skill. Live rank comes from lap and ordered checkpoints, which also block shortcuts. Barriers deflect and slow instead of stopping. First across lap 2 wins; otherwise placement and time read as a loss.

Three vehicles trade top speed, handling and ram mass. Mid-key sunlit world: one shadow-casting key, fog-blended sky dome, barriers and instanced scatter, multi-part vehicles not bare primitives on an empty plane; speed-scaled radial streaks from the vanishing point carry velocity.

Lanternroot Reaches, a third-person 3D quest-exploration adventure (Three.js/WebGL2). Camera: ~6.5u behind and 3.2u above the avatar, pitched ~18° down, damped soft-follow with yaw auto-aligning behind travel, no free-look, blended transitions rather than hard cuts. Controls: arrows/WASD camera-relative on the flattened ground plane (Up drives into the screen, Left/Right never invert), Space for a weighty ~1.8u-apex jump that clears the widest 2.6u gap with a landing settle, left-click to collect or activate hovered in-range targets. Loop: accept the glowkeeper statue's task, traverse ledges and gaps, hover-ring then click pulsing glimmerseeds in vantage-gated nooks, click the lever once its seed prerequisite is met so the sealed gate opens and the arena portal appears (unmet shows a lock cue and condition), then fight a best-of-3 tag duel against a magenta rival sharing your movement kit, scorable only in its telegraphed vulnerable window. Win and loss both grant glow-shards and route through a result summary to Continue (Ruin Stair-Halls: wider gaps, faster windows) or Restart; totals persist in localStorage, and out-of-bounds falls respawn at the last safe node with nothing lost. Matte desaturated stone-and-moss scenes (dusk-teal grove, slate-violet ruin) reserve warm amber emissive for seeds, active mechanisms and the portal, cyan avatar against magenta rival; fogged three-zone depth, with instanced scatter, glow-pollen and swaying foliage filling camera dead zones instead of a flat empty plane.

Real-time 2D siege tactics on a fixed oblique top-down screen: deploy zone left, ash lanes center, layered keep right. Buy tank/anti-armor/ranged/ram units under a Supply budget, place them, then click to move or attack; breach the gate, then the ember-lit core, within 120s.

2D side-view auto-run brawler on storm-lit floating stone causeways. The hero jumps and steers past hazards until a gate halts the scroll behind a barrier; stone guardians fall to 3-hit light chains and combo arts, then the run resumes faster and denser. 3 hits end it; score = distance + combo kills.

Build Fracture City Outlaw, a 3D open-world urban action sandbox in React + Vite on Three.js/WebGL2. Pick one of three stat-biased rogues; spawn into one contiguous concrete-and-glass district. Camera: third-person trailing rig, distance 8 on foot, 12 driving, 360° yaw by mouse drag or A/D, pitch clamped −35° to +12°, damped follow that never clips geometry, re-parenting on vehicle enter/exit. Controls: WASD moves camera-relative — A/Left screen-left, W/Up screen-forward, never inverted or axis-swapped; Space clears authored ledges; click fires the aimed tool; 1/2/3 swap breaker, launcher, pry-tool; E accepts missions and enters/exits vehicles. Loop: accept the active chain mission, travel on foot or by commandeered car, strike mission-eligible structures, matching tool to concrete, metal or glass, until integrity empties into a post-damage silhouette with debris and a fracture-reveal material exposing dark aggregate and rebar; destruction raises heat through four tiers spawning drones then faster cruisers; breaking line of sight ~4s decays heat; then spend currency on upgrades. Pursuer hits drain status; zero fails the mission to a result screen with retry. Three chained missions, then persistent free roam. Keep the city desaturated grey with saturated accents only on rogue, targets and vehicles, reserve #FF3B30 for pursuit including an edge-only vignette scaling per tier, and layer street props and window-lit towers under one shadow-casting sun with ambient motion, no empty plane.

3D browser aerial creature combat in Three.js/WebGL2, one full-viewport canvas: pilot a winged wyrm through a sky arena of floating islands, dueling enemy beasts. Camera: damped third-person chase ~9u behind and 4u above the beast, tightening in banks, widening at speed, biasing toward a locked enemy and pulling in when islands occlude; never invert, cut, or lose the beast. Controls: tap/hold anywhere steers toward that projected point — a tap on the visible right banks right, higher or lower taps pitch up or down within clamps; breath auto-fires on cooldown at the nearest enemy in the forward cone, and tapping an on-screen enemy lunges into a contact strike. Loop: loot essence motes and rarer relics in free flight → wave combat with hit-stop and brief invulnerability per hit → spend essence between waves on four cultivation nodes (health, breath damage, breath cooldown, lunge reach) that visibly grow scale, spines and emissive vents and persist across runs → next wave. Three escalating waves: two basics, three strafers, then a beam-charging elite with an escort; clearing all wins, zero health loses, results offer retry or a fresh run keeping progression. Mist rings the ~260u playfield and pushes the beast inside. Warm sun key, cool ambient, fog and shadows; foreground spurs, midground islands and arches, multi-tier cloud banks and a ringed celestial body, all in slow drift — never flat empty sky or a tiled 2D backdrop. Player, enemies and treasure each keep an exclusive accent hue and shape; HUD neutral.

2D side-on: hold to ascend, release to fall, forward drift automatic. Contact eats anything at or below your tier; larger ends the run. Energy evolves you bigger, making former predators edible and opening deadlier regions with high-reward rivals. Muted parallax canyon, bold-outlined creatures.
Flat 2D fill-in-the-blank puzzle: type the missing word; two misses reveal it and advance. Streak scoring, bot leaderboard, white reading card on a neutral field.

Build "Pillowpuff Haven," a tap-only virtual-pet care sim in a true 3D cozy interior (Three.js) under one locked camera: three-quarter front view pitched ~22° down onto the active creature, never orbiting, panning, zooming, or following. Taps raycast onto fixed floor/wall planes — tap Feed/Play/Clean then the creature or zone, tap it to pet, drag only to reposition décor. Hunger, Energy, Cleanliness and Mood decay in real time toward a soft floor, applied on resume via saved timestamp; care and petting restore needs and add ever-rising affection; happiness = weighted need satisfaction plus décor bonuses; affection thresholds advance three growth stages. Party mode keeps the same pose, festively relit, granting bonuses and sometimes a companion who joins the roster. Neglect never fails you: it softens expression and one tap recovers. Rounded plush chibi creatures with soft rim sheen in a high-luminance warm-neutral room; focal props may use richer beveled geometry.

Procedural pixel-art side-view brawler on cool neon-city parallax. Camera locks horizontally until a wave clears, then scrolls right. Punch, Kick, Block, Jump; Punch-Punch-Kick knocks down; held Block fails against Guard-Break. Three stages end in telegraphed bosses.

Build "Sunberry Sprint", a browser 3D lane runner in Three.js: a harvest cart auto-runs down one orchard lane while the player steers only laterally, gathering sunberries that visibly stack in its basket (cap 60). Loop: gates and loose berries grow the stack → hazards cost 4 units with a red flash and brief slowdown, never a loss → four pass-through arches convert the whole stack in fixed order raw→rinsed→sorted→pressed→bottled without changing its count → at the finish each bottled unit packs one-to-one into a crate jar; score is jar count, best yield persisted in localStorage. Camera: chase rig at cart-local offset (0, 4.2, −7.5), pitched −14°, look-at 6 units ahead, damped lateral follow, no orbit or zoom, fog near 220 units. Controls: mouse or touch drag maps to lane offset along the camera-right vector, so dragging left always moves the cart screen-left. Bright rounded casual-arcade daylight; foreground branches, midground lane props, pastel hills with barn and turning windmill; instanced scenery so no stretch reads as an empty plane. Per-instance berry material cross-fades hue, roughness and translucency across the five states; warm bloom keyed to the emissive jars only at the finish.

2D pass-and-play hidden-role deduction on a slate dossier table: all seats but one infiltrator share a secret location, each card seen only by its holder. One question per turn; the answerer asks next, never back. A one-shot vote or guess ends it; expiry favors him.

3D Three.js/WebGL2 stealth capture: an oversized night warden subdues three masked prowlers in a lamplit dusk lodge and hauls each to a paddy wagon; two escapes through its single exit door lose the run.

Camera: third-person rig above and behind the warden; mouse-drag orbits yaw, pitch clamped 12–48°, wheel distance 4.5–8.0, yaw easing back behind when idle; a spring-arm raycast stops clipping and blocking walls fade. Controls: WASD is camera-relative — A moves screen-left, W away from camera; Shift sneaks quiet; E is the only context verb — search, use, disable, grab, deliver.

Loop: read patrol routes, then close in unseen or ambush a chokepoint. A 0–100 detection meter fills in each prowler's vision cone, scaled by your noise, and decays behind cover; at 100 it acts by type — calm patroller flees then resumes, panicky one hides, exit-rusher beelines for the door. E grabs an in-range target, carried limp at reduced speed until a trap stuns you and forces a drop that revives it. Single-slot consumables open routes or extend a grab.

Visuals: layered beveled lodge rooms — staircase, fireplace, bookshelf, piano — cool teal dusk fill under amber lamp pools, one shadow-casting moonlight, fog in the exit hall, constant embers and dust; warden teal and prowler magenta never bleed into environment or UI.
Fixed side-on 2D court, flat vector with teal lines: sixty seconds versus an AI rival, one point per basket, distance and angle set makes, spacing beyond block range beats swats.

Fixed-camera 2D dominoes on deep-teal felt: two players (AI or hot-seat) extend one linear chain by matching pips at either open end, drawing when stuck; the winner scores the loser's pips toward a target.

Hexanova: Number Bloom — an endless single-screen hex number-merge puzzle in a true 3D Three.js/WebGL scene, never flat 2D: beveled hex prisms with matte flat tops in the recessed wells of a muted teal board, soft contact shadows, slate backdrop. Camera: one fixed perspective tilted ~55° down, locked on board center, framing the radius-4 pointy-top 61-cell grid and queue tray in 16:9; no orbit, pan, or zoom, only a ≤220 ms cascade shake that returns to the exact pose. Controls: pointer raycast onto the fixed board plane; tap a tile, then tap an empty cell reachable through contiguous empty cells; invalid targets cost no turn. Loop: move → any connected group of four or more equal tiles under six-neighbour adjacency collapses into one next-tier tile at the moved tile's cell → re-scan and cascade with a rising multiplier → the front of a five-value preview queue drops into a random empty cell, possibly cascading → refill the queue; pulse a warning below 20% empty cells. Eight tiers 2–256 climb a cool-to-warm ramp to a metallic top tier; numerals contrast-flip to stay legible. Saturation (no legal move, no cell for the drop) ends the run: dim the board and show score, highest tile, best, and restart.

Head-on 2D drop-and-merge puzzle: aim horizontally and drop faceted gems into a glass basin; same-tier contacts merge one tier up and chain for score; a gem settling above the overflow line ends the run.

Top-down 2D arena: your mouse-steered rover and three AI rivals never stop, laying lethal trails outside owned territory; close a loop to fill it; any crossed trail kills its owner. Follow-camera; glowing trails on grey grid.

Endless 3D free-roam drift-driving sandbox in Three.js/WebGL2. Pick one of three fictional coupes (Speed/Grip/Handling trade-offs), then roam a loopable dusk metropolis of multi-lane avenues and an elevated highway ribbon with neutral lane-following AI traffic. Camera: chase ~6.5u behind and 2.8u above, pitched 9° down, damped position/yaw follow; C blends chase→hood→cockpit→orbit, and screen-left/right must never invert against steering in any view. Controls: WASD/arrows steer and throttle/brake-reverse, Space handbrake, F nitro, 1/2/3 economy/drift-lean/sport tunings that measurably shift grip and throttle. Loop: weave traffic, break rear grip with handbrake or drift mode, hold a slip-angle window to accrue drift score while contact-free near-misses tick a combo multiplier that scales all gains and decays when idle; a collision resets the combo with a red-orange desaturation flash, and a hard wreck soft-respawns the car upright and lane-aligned nearby, run continuing. No game-over, only personal bests for score, longest drift and top speed. Visuals: teal-to-indigo dusk sky, charcoal asphalt, concrete-and-neon skyline with warm lamp pools, one setting-sun key light with soft shadows; the coupe is the sole saturated electric-cyan object, with violet-blue nitro plume, warm-grey tire smoke and skid marks; layer foreground props, midground traffic and background skyline so no bare plane shows. Focal props may use richer beveled geometry.

2D top-down 1-bit roguelite shooter, 384×216 integer-scaled. WASD moves, arrows fire eight-way, Space dashes invulnerably. Clear locked rooms, draft power-ups, cross four motifs to multi-phase bosses; death banks coins into unlocks. Camera clamps at room bounds; walls are dither-shaded white on black; red marks only hazards and life; lethal attacks telegraph.

Build a browser evidence-deduction investigation game in 2.5D: lit low-poly faceted 3D dioramas with real bevels and frame corners closed by geometry, never bare planes — a timber lodge, a wet concrete yard with cars and conifers, an archive annex — while dialogue and UI stay unlit flat vector, and the two material languages never mix. Camera: one fixed read-only pose per site, ~10 m up at ~40° pitch, three-quarter overhead, whole space in one frame; no orbit, pan or zoom, site switches are fades, any impact shake returning to the exact pose. Click markers and cards, drag evidence into numbered slots; markers sit in a constant-size overlay raycast to bounding boxes. Loop: search each fixed frame for 6–8 one-shot markers, some decoys and a few hidden until the matching trace or handwriting method is active, spent ones dimming to imprints → filed evidence carries tags → tags unlock interview topics until a character states a flawed claim → cross-examination, where the unordered slot set must equal the solution exactly and partial hits fail without naming the gap. Five attempts, hints escalating; at zero roll back to the pre-rebuttal checkpoint, refill attempts, keep evidence and tally a mistake. The first upheld rebuttal opens the third site; the case ends by accusing a suspect with three key exhibits, graded on clue coverage and mistakes. Every solution tag must be collectable before its rebuttal fires.

Point-and-click 2D mystery in a storm-lashed manor: fixed camera, oblique duotone slate-blue pixel interiors. Click to walk, examine hotspots, combine items, question guests with choices that shift affinity, and drag a receiver onto a drifting signal band; clues gate locked rooms, and two irreversible choices plus the final accusation pick one of three endings.

Three.js 2.5D: a first-person compliance officer sorts attestation forms against shifting corporate directives over three escalating workdays. Camera: fixed perspective seated at the desk, angled down at the CRT and trays; no orbit, pan or zoom, only a brief misfile shake returning to pose. Controls: pointer only, raycast onto the fixed desk plane; click a form to raise it toward the camera, drag it onto a tray. Loop: a low-res windowed OS on the CRT pushes each day's judgment rules, some mutually contradictory; forms carry tampered or missing fields; cross-check its Registry, Manual and Notes apps so exactly one of CLEAR, SANCTION or ELEVATE is correct; clear the quota, with a single recall of the last filed form, while three misfiles in a day means dismissal. Flat cel-shaded colleague standees interrupt to beg exceptions; replies shift a relation value and an obedience-conscience axis deciding a loyalist, defector or dismissed ending. Three depths must read: foreground desk clutter, the warm-wood desk as the sole warm light pool, and a cold blue near-black cubicle receding past fluorescent panels, partitions and distant workstations. Faint VHS aberration, scanlines and grain persist over CRT phosphor glow and spike on misfile and climax; no flat 2D substitute or bare primitives.

2D pixel-art card dungeon: empty a shuffled deck in 4-card rooms, resolving 3 and carrying 1 over. A weapon that kills value X may then only strike lower monsters; bare hands cost full value from 20 hearts. Clicks only, camera fixed on a card table over a muted path.

Build a browser wave-arena action RPG in Three.js/WebGL: a cel-shaded, ink-outlined champion carves through hordes across three dark, saturated realms (steel colosseum, magenta conduit, spore-lit wastes). Real 3D staged 2.5D on a lateral plane: glossy reflective floor, per-realm colored fog, layered depth framing a clear lane. Camera: fixed perspective, FOV 42, at [0,4.5,12] looking at [0,2.2,0]; never orbit, pan, zoom or follow; only brief hit shake decaying back to the exact pose. Controls: A/D slides the fighter along the plane; 1–6 cast energy-gated actives on cooldowns; x1/x3/x5/x12 speed uniformly scales attacks, cooldowns, energy regen and enemy actions. Loop: in a cool-blue hub, equip gear and spend stat and skill points, enter an unlocked realm, auto-attack the nearest enemy while casting, clear waves into a 2.5x boss, then bank XP and rarity-tiered gear with rolled affixes; each clear unlocks the next realm, and prestige resets progress for a permanent stacking XP multiplier. 0 HP returns to the hub with progress intact; keep silhouettes separable on every realm.

Build "Puffkin Vale", a cozy third-person 3D creature-catching collectathon in Three.js/WebGL2 with a true movable camera, not a fixed 2.5D view. Camera: damped spring-arm over-the-shoulder at 4–6m with obstruction pull-in, free 360° yaw, pitch clamped -8° to +45°. Controls: camera-relative WASD (A/D screen-left/right, never inverted), mouse orbit, Space dive-scoop, E interact. Loop: a market-pavilion keeper issues one errand at a time; dashed hand-drawn ground outlines mark targets; Puffkins wander until you enter their awareness radius, then flee, rare glowing ones sensing farther and dodging sharper; a dive catches only inside a front cone at close range, else it whiffs and the chase resumes, no penalty or death; each catch logs a codex trait line; handing in a full errand retracts a vine gate into a shaded grove; after the last hand-in, reaching the distant Great Boughspire plays a reunion ending, then free-roam. Persist progress locally. Every orbit angle composes painterly matte layers: foreground overhanging leaves and root arches, grass-tufted paths, roaming Puffkins and a lantern-hung pavilion midground, giant canopy and the Boughspire under one seamless sky dome; warm clearings against cool groves, wind-swayed grass, cyan glow only on rares. No bare planes or default primitives.

Build "Wayforge: Frontier Reclamation" in React + Three.js: a hand-painted 2.5D diorama of real 3D toon-banded stacked platforms, bridges and stairs. Camera: fixed orthographic isometric, 3/4 overhead, framing the whole level; no orbit, pan, zoom or follow. Controls: pointer only — click an interactable and the nearest idle worker walks there, works, returns; click a running task to cancel and refund; extra tasks queue and reorder (pool 3, cap 5 via housing). Loop: gather wood, food, gold, stone, crystal from depleting nodes, spend them clearing obstacles and repairing bridges and stairs that open new platforms with fresh nodes and build points, then build and upgrade mill, farm, well, warehouse, housing and blacksmith for food, gather speed and caps. Snow bonfires must be lit with wood before clearing. Objectives tick live; all met clears the level with a time medal; only timed levels can fail into retry. Biome shifts change only environment color and key-light warmth. Keep foreground occlusion, a midground play area and a background cliff silhouette, corners filled, no empty flat plane.

Top-down 2D pixel horror: explore a rainy graveyard hub and three haunted houses where a flickering lantern radius alone reveals what you can see or touch; contact starts turn-based combat, and clearing all three opens a protect-or-join ending.

Flat 2D visual-novel life sim, fixed camera: full-bleed painted backdrop, stat sidebar. Click map nodes to spend three daily slots over 28 days; actions trade Energy and Money for skills, dialogue raises three characters' affection, and thresholds decide one of four endings.

Flat 2D browser music tool: any keypress on the computer keyboard yields a consonant note or chord, and changing chord or tonality live remaps the whole key→pitch table. Held keys stack as voices lighting a piano strip and staff; record and replay takes, plus a memory-echo mode.

Build a browser Three.js game: a turn-based match-3 weapon-forging dungeon battler, 2.5D in a true 3D scene. Camera: orthographic isometric ~40°, fixed on a central 7×7 board with enemies in an upper background band — no orbit, pan, or zoom, only a ≤6px hit shake returning exactly to pose. Controls: tap a cell then an adjacent one to swap (taps ray-cast to the board plane), tap a forged weapon then a living enemy to throw, End Turn. Loop: match 3+ gems of four material categories, clear and refill, cascades raising tier; each clear forges a weapon prop with an attack value into one of 4 slots (full slots block forging); when swaps run out the throw phase subtracts that value and applies fire burn / ice skipped turn / poison drain; then procedurally generated enemies act by AI on the hero, until one side is wiped. A multi-phase boss ends a district and offers one of three run-only boons or gold; hero HP ≤0 ends the run, clearing boons but keeping attributes, ember-bought weapon mastery, and unlocks. Visuals: bold black outlines and high-saturation flat cel-shading over a volumetric stone dungeon — near-black slate lit by warm-orange torch point-lights, board zone brightened, foreground pillars and chains, background arches and a colossal cold furnace. No flat 2D planes, empty ground, or default primitives.

2D top-down tile RPG; every creature is seed-generated: sprite, stats, moves. Camera follows the player, clamped at map edges. Tall-grass steps roll encounters; SPD-ordered turns; capture odds rise as HP drops; fuse two team creatures into a glitch-blended hybrid. Boss badges seed the next world; wipes recover at spawn. Handheld pixel art; neutral near-black UI over random creature colors.
